name: Jaxen Cepeda
strengths: Cepeda (#74) finishes through the whistle as a true tackle — drives legs after contact and buries edge defenders in the run game.
Cepeda delivers a heavy initial punch and latches; once locked, he torques defenders out of the gap instead of catching.
Cepeda climbs cleanly to the second level on screens and outside zone, taking angles and finishing on LBs in space.
Cepeda shows functional kick-slide depth and can drop his hips to stall bull rush when the set is on time.
weaknesses: Cepeda still pops high out of his stance in pass pro — higher pad level will get long-armed by SEC edge speed until leverage tightens.
Cepeda occasionally stops his feet and lunges on contact — over-extension invites swim/push-pull until the base stays under him.
comparison: Cepeda comps to Dalton Risner — 6-4 / 6-5 power-finisher OL mold; OT snaps with heavy hands and nasty run displacement that project cleanly to IOL/swing-tackle mass at the next level (size-matched to Cepeda's 6-4.5 / 290 frame).
projection: Cepeda projects as develop Year 1, earn Year 2-3 SEC rotation snaps at OT/OG. Ceiling: multi-year starter upside as an interior mauler or swing tackle — the Greenwood finisher who can grow into every-down P4 value.
schemeFit: Cepeda fits a power/zone hybrid OL room that wants finish and second-level climb, with IOL flex if length limits pure edge vs elite speed.

insiderNotes: Cepeda is a 6-4.5 / 290 Greenwood tackle who wins with heavy hands, finish, and second-level mobility. Pad level and base maintenance are the growth items — mold is OT with clean IOL flex.
